Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Anne-Louise-Germaine Staël (author, Wikidata Q123041), died 1817; Albertine-Adrienne Necker de Saussure (other, Wikidata Q2375310), died 1841; Charles Augustin Sainte-Beuve (other, Wikidata Q1063392), died 1869. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Staël, Madame de (Anne-Louise-Germaine), 1766-1817; Necker de Saussure, Albertine-Adrienne, 1766-1841 [Contributor]; Sainte-Beuve, Charles Augustin, 1804-1869 [Contributor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Corinne, ou, l'Italie, Paris : Firmin-Didot, 1877, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/corinneoulital00sta. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 93%, 93%, 88% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Albertine-Adrienne Necker de Saussure, Charles Augustin Sainte-Beuve, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
